result.summary: The image shows a wide urban arterial road with four travel lanes and signalized intersections. While sidewalks and basic crossing infrastructure are present, the environment is heavily oriented toward vehicle throughput with long crossing distances and minimal pedestrian protection.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four travel lanes plus parking lanes at the intersection, increasing exposure time to traffic.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the sidewalk path, reducing the effective clear width for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace standard transverse markings with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with a painted center buffer, which likely facilitates high vehicle speeds. While sidewalks are present, the lack of physical buffers, long crossing distances, and large stretches of blank frontage create a relatively hostile environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to spend a significant amount of time exposed to traffic when crossing at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area on the left side of the frame

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Multiple wide travel lanes and a lack of physical traffic calming measures encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The large vacant lot reduces natural surveillance and 'eyes on the street', which can impact perceived pedestrian safety.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left background, adjacent to the sidewalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised concrete refuge island in the center median to allow pedestrians to cross the wide road in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Plant street trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical buffer from traffic and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane arterial road with four through lanes and on-street parking, creating a high-speed environment for vehicles. While sidewalks are present on both sides, there is a complete lack of pedestrian crossing infrastructure, refuge islands, or traffic calming measures visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: A pedestrian attempting to cross would have to traverse at least four travel lanes and two parking lanes without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the entire roadway width

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Multiple wide, straight travel lanes with minimal friction or narrowing encourage high vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes extending toward the horizon

hazards.name: Blank Frontage and Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: The right side of the street consists of a large paved area with billboards and no physical buffer between the walkway and high-speed traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a line of street trees and a furniture zone to provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a very wide commercial driveway that creates a significant gap in the sidewalk's protection. Pedestrians must navigate a large, undefined conflict zone where vehicles enter and exit a fast-food parking lot without clear priority or markings.

hazards.name: Excessive Driveway Width
hazards.description: The extremely wide curb cut for the parking lot entrance increases the exposure time for pedestrians to turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center, spanning the width of the parking lot entrance

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Continuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk material and level are not maintained across the driveway, failing to clearly define a safe path for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, where the concrete sidewalk meets the asphalt driveway

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the curb cut to the minimum necessary for safe vehicle access, shortening the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Treatment
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk material and grade across the driveway to reinforce pedestrian priority and slow entering vehicles.

interventions.title: Wayfinding and Markings
interventions.description: Add high-visibility markings across the driveway to alert drivers to the presence of a pedestrian walkway.
